profile.campus: San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas (CyrusOne San Antonio campus, SAT2-SAT4)
profile.address: 9554-9655 Westover Hills Blvd / Raba Drive, San Antonio, TX 78251
profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, the SAT2-SAT4 campus spans two addresses: SAT2-SAT3 at 9554 Westover Hills Boulevard, San Antonio, TX 78251, and SAT4 at 9655 Raba Drive, San Antonio, TX 78251, totaling 295,785 sq ft and 36 MW of IT capacity across the three buildings.

CyrusOne's first San Antonio facility opened in 2012; per CyrusOne's own press release on its fifth San Antonio campus (SAT5-SAT6, broken ground January 2025 in Texas Research Park), the company had invested approximately $1 billion in capital to date across its San Antonio campuses as of that release, and describes SAT5-SAT6 itself as two buildings totaling 276,000 sq ft and 36 MW of IT capacity, figures that differ somewhat from an earlier operator-page-sourced figure of 175,000 sq ft/33 MW recorded for that campus elsewhere in this registry, a discrepancy noted rather than silently reconciled. The San Antonio Report, a local nonprofit newsroom, reported in 2026 that the city hosts more than 20 operational data centers with 59 more in various planning stages; CPS Energy, the municipally owned utility, supplies power to 21 of the existing facilities (generating roughly $110 million in revenue) and has projected future data center energy demand in the metro at approximately 26,000 megawatts, while flagging water use as a growing constraint: data centers currently draw about 0.1% of San Antonio Water System's drinking water, but planned new facilities have requested roughly 600 acre-feet of drinking water and 3,000 acre-feet of recycled water against a system that has capacity for only about 10,000 additional acre-feet before requiring upgrades.

CyrusOne's San Antonio growth mirrors a broader pattern across Texas, where absence of a state corporate income tax, relatively low land and construction costs compared to Northern Virginia or Silicon Valley, and CPS Energy's municipal-utility rate structure have made the metro attractive to colocation and hyperscale operators alike; San Antonio's data center footprint has grown alongside comparable buildouts in Dallas-Fort Worth (where CyrusOne's Carrollton facility, opened in 2012, was described by the company as the largest data center in Texas at the time) and Austin.

sources.title: San Antonio has over 20 data centers and more on the way

profile.research_note: Cowork facility-page writer 2026-09-03: rebuilt from a 2026-09-02 legacy profile shape; added San Antonio Report's 2026 CPS Energy/SAWS water-and-power coverage and CyrusOne's own SAT5-SAT6 groundbreaking press release as sources and campus history.

reading.body:
Among Texas data centers that publish capacity, the CyrusOne San Antonio campus ranks fourth at 36 MW, representing roughly 11 percent of the eight facilities' combined 315 MW total. This single campus could support approximately 900 GPU-dense racks at typical AI training power densities, or 3,600 racks at enterprise densities, yet operators across Texas publish capacity figures for less than 10 percent of mapped facilities, making the true regional total invisible.

The campus holds certifications across payment processing, healthcare, information security, and federal workloads. These qualify it to host regulated data but do not indicate current tenancy. The lack of individual building breakdowns means the 36 MW cannot be attributed to specific structures on the two adjacent parcels.

CyrusOne operates this campus as part of a larger Texas footprint spanning San Antonio, Austin, and the Dallas Fort Worth cluster anchored in Carrollton. The company has traded ownership through acquisition, IPO, and leveraged buyout over two decades, cycling from private to public and back to private in 2022 at a 15 billion dollar valuation. The San Antonio campus has run as a long-standing Texas market presence without a documented opening story in available sources, suggesting stability but limited visibility into when capacity was built or how it has scaled.
